name: Patriotic Socialism
summary: Patriotic socialism, or socialist patriotism, is the Marxist-Leninist doctrine that love of country and defence of the socialist state are compatible with, and even an expression of, proletarian internationalism. It separates proletarian patriotism from bourgeois nationalism and chauvinism, supports the self-determination of oppressed nations, and ties loyalty to the nation to loyalty to the socialist system and the ruling party.
scope: The Marxist-Leninist strand as documented in Lenin's 1914 essay on Great-Russian national pride, Mao's 1938 report on patriotism and internationalism, and the state practice summarised in Wikipedia (Soviet Union under Stalin, China, Vietnam, East Germany, Yugoslavia, Cuba, North Korea, Ethiopia). It does not cover the pre-1914 social-patriotic parties that backed their own governments in the First World War, nor right-wing national socialism.

furtherReading.title: Socialist patriotism (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: Overview of the doctrine and its use in Soviet, Chinese, Vietnamese and other states.

furtherReading.title: Lenin, On the National Pride of the Great Russians
furtherReading.note: The classic statement of non-chauvinist national pride within socialism.

furtherReading.title: Mao, The Role of the Chinese Communist Party in the National War
furtherReading.note: Argues that communists must combine patriotism with internationalism.

keyFigures.name: Vladimir Lenin
keyFigures.role: Separated proletarian patriotism from chauvinism and defended national self-determination.

keyFigures.name: Mao Zedong
keyFigures.role: Defined Chinese communist patriotism as applied internationalism in 1938.

keyFigures.name: Joseph Stalin
keyFigures.role: Promoted socialist patriotism under socialism in one country.

sources.title: Socialist patriotism
sources.author: Wikipedia

sources.title: On the National Pride of the Great Russians (1914)
sources.author: V. I. Lenin
sources.usedFor: Non-slavish national pride, rejection of chauvinism, self-determination, class versus nation.

sources.author: Mao Zedong

sources.title: Marxism-Leninism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Planned economy, state ownership, vanguard party, state atheism, class doctrine that socialist patriotism operates within.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Socialist states under this banner treated health care as a public service funded by the state, in line with state control of the economy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Mao's report calls for policies that protect workers' livelihoods, and a socialist state sets pay itself, so firm wage floors fit; a substantial raise is not specifically documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states replaced market allocation with state planning and public ownership, so adherents deny that markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: Marxist-Leninist practice, which socialist patriotism serves, puts the means of production under state control, including energy, rail and utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: A socialist state aims to curb the propertied classes, so heavy taxation of the wealthy follows from its class politics.

unions-good.rationale: Mao's report wants workers protected and organised in the national struggle, but unions work under party leadership rather than independently.

property-fundamental.rationale: Socialist ownership of the means of production overrides private property, which is not treated as an inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Where private firms exist the socialist state subordinates them to national plans, so tighter regulation is the default stance.

cut-welfare.rationale: Socialist states built social provision as a core duty, so cutting welfare for dependency reasons is rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist ownership is by the state or collectives in the workers' name; direct worker ownership of each firm is sympathetic but not the usual form.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Ruling parties in these states accepted extensive security surveillance, but the sources do not discuss terrorism, so the answer is an extrapolation.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Socialist-patriotic states treated drug use as social decay and punished it, though no source here states a position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: These movements condemn chauvinism and racialism and states such as East Germany and Ethiopia suppressed them, which supports legal limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Leader-centred party states in the Soviet, North Korean and Chinese cases promoted strong leadership, though framed as the party's rather than a gridlock-bypassing individual.

state-harmful.rationale: Marxist-Leninists seek a strong state during the transition, and socialist patriotism loyalty to the state and system is a core duty.

limit-guns.rationale: Socialist states restrict private arms ownership in practice, but sources do not discuss gun policy directly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Defence of the socialist fatherland is central, and these states put heavy emphasis on the army and security organs.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socialist states generally treated prostitution as exploitation to be abolished, but this is not stated in the sources used.

decide-locally.rationale: Lenin said he favoured centralisation over federalism other conditions being equal, and party states run from the centre.

rehabilitation.rationale: Socialist penal theory stressed re-education through labour, though no source here addresses prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents split between Soviet and Chinese states that promoted family stability and ones that reformed it; the sources are silent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Most self-described socialist-patriotic states historically opposed it, but sources do not discuss it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Most Marxist-Leninist states legalised abortion, though some pronatalist cases differed; sources are silent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states practised state atheism, so adherents would not want religion to play a larger public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents oppose racialism and chauvinism and back oppressed peoples' liberation, but domestic race remedies are not a stated theme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources do not address gender theory, and communist parties differ on it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mao's report calls for giving Marxism a Chinese form and studying national history from Confucius to Sun Yat-sen, tying socialism to national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Lenin and Mao defend revolution and decisive action, so adherents reject a requirement that change be gradual and bound by established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Adherents reject chauvinism and xenophobia and stress internationalism, though socialist states controlled migration tightly.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They hold proletarian internationalism together with state sovereignty and have been wary of Western-led bodies; no clear stance.

free-trade.rationale: Planned socialist economies controlled foreign trade through the state, so adherents do not credit free trade with benefiting all.

nation-first.rationale: Mao treats patriotism as applied internationalism, so national interest is pursued without rejecting global solidarity; adherents lean towards national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Mao and the tradition support national liberation wars, but oppose imperialist intervention under humanitarian cover.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are expected to remain in the socialist states they defend, and eventual open borders belongs to a distant communist future.

limit-growth.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states pursued rapid industrialisation and growth, so limiting growth for environmental reasons is not their line.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Planned states can direct drastic action, but the sources do not mention climate.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Socialist states stressed scientific and technological progress as the foundation of socialism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Socialist-patriotic states built nuclear power and weapons, though no source here speaks to energy policy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lenin celebrates the 1905 working-class movement and urges workers to act against their own ruling class, and Mao's tradition rests on revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Vanguard theory gives leadership to the party rather than to experts or the public as such.

central-planning.rationale: The planned economy is a defining feature of the Marxist-Leninist model that socialist patriotism upholds.

socialized-markets.rationale: Reform socialists such as China and Vietnam accept markets under public ownership, while orthodox adherents reject them.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a socialist programme item; socialist states nationalise or collectivise land rather than tax its value.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Abolishing or heavily taxing inherited property fits the socialist attack on propertied classes.

basic-income.rationale: Socialist states link income to work and provide services rather than unconditional cash.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: State control of trade protects domestic industry in socialist economies, though not as a free-standing tariff doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State planning of investment toward heavy and strategic industry is central to the model.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Socialist ownership aims at public property, not wide diffusion among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds that money and wages disappear only under full communism, a distant goal that socialist states did not pursue now.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Socialist states run banking through the state and have no wish to leave money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Economic coordination is by state planning under the party, not by negotiated bodies of employers and workers.

one-party-rule.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states are run by a vanguard party, and the Chinese version casts the government as embodying the people's will.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Lenin's essay praises Radishchev and Decembrist resistance to tsarism, and socialist states are republics.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents prefer socialist democracy led by the party to multiparty electoralism where voters can choose badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Democratic centralism rather than referenda is the organising principle of these states.

workers-councils.rationale: The soviet idea gave councils a founding role, but in later practice party-state institutions displaced them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin supported the right of oppressed nations to self-determination, though Soviet and Chinese practice repressed separatism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Lenin's equality doctrine rejects hereditary or innate rulership, though a vanguard is a leading elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lenin calls for being ready to shoot one's own ruling classes and Mao fights a war, so political violence is not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: Mao's wartime writings call for national consciousness to be built through war, but adherents do not hold war as ennobling in itself.

separate-church-state.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states formally separated church from state while subordinating religion to the party.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states practise state atheism and base law on party and socialist principles.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence and law enforcement are state duties, and socialist patriotism centres on defending the fatherland through the state.

military-superiority.rationale: Mao stresses a strong national defence against aggression, but the tradition also argues for peaceful coexistence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The article describes a civic, multi-ethnic nation under Mao, condemns Han chauvinism, and Ethiopia and others rejected racialism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mao says class struggle is real and must be adjusted rather than denied, in line with the Marxist view of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialism aims at abolishing class distinctions and distributing by labour then need, so equality of outcome is favoured as a goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Sources do not address indigenous land claims; socialist states differ.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Lenin condemns national oppression and the tradition backs anti-colonial struggle, but reparations are not documented as a demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: Adherents tie unity to class and socialist system rather than shared religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialist ethics subordinate personal interest to the collective, as the CCP's first level of patriotism puts it.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The CCP defines patriotism as subordinating personal interests to the state, the socialist system and communism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Sources are silent, and socialist states treated nature largely as a resource.

limit-population.rationale: China enforced population limits while the USSR promoted births, so adherents differ.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marxism-Leninism builds on industrialisation as the base of socialism and rejects the claim that it is a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Socialist states pressed for rapid technical modernisation, though under party control rather than disruptive of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed, and socialist states had no common position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed in any source consulted; adherents would defer to the party.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Party states control communications, but no source here covers encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Lenin looks to progress through socialism and rejects tsarism; adherents do not set restoring a lost order above progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats ideology as the guide to policy, though reform factions stress pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Party and state organisation rather than spontaneous direct action is the route to change.

means-match-ends.rationale: Lenin treats shooting at one's own ruling classes as a legitimate means to socialism, so means need not mirror the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marxism-Leninism builds on industrial development and has no place for a return to hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx envisions its abolition under communism, but it is a far-off aim for socialist states.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is the communist stage's principle, which socialism points toward but does not yet practise.

production-for-use.rationale: Planned economies are designed to meet social needs rather than private profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist analysis of surplus value is the standard theory adherents hold.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The transition under working-class state power over former ruling classes is the standard Marxist-Leninist doctrine.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation was the model in the USSR and China, though later reform periods allowed household farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin treats the 1914 war as an imperialist conflict between capitalist powers and condemns those who back it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Socialist states rest on state revenue to finance public services.

harm-principle.rationale: The state directs social and cultural life rather than restricting itself to preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The tradition stresses collective and class interests and duties over individual rights alone.

conscription.rationale: Mao's mobilisation of the nation and the defence of the socialist fatherland support conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Loyalty to the nation and system is a core duty, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is an instrument of socialist construction, not a firm with citizen-customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Socialist states stress material guarantees such as work, housing and health as the basis of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold that the party leads culture and media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The ideology condemns racialism, as in the Derg and the rejection of chauvinism the article records.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through the party and soviets, not through families and local communities.

total-state.rationale: Party states directed culture, education and the economy, though adherents would not use the word total.

national-rebirth.rationale: Socialist patriotism celebrates national resistance and construction but not a rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lenin condemns subjugating other peoples as defence of the fatherland, so expansion is rejected.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Lenin's praise of resistance to autocracy and the party-state model contradict rule by personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Lenin celebrates liberation from tsarist oppression and the tradition is hostile to serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism treats ideology as class-bound, but Soviet-style adherents claim a scientific truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Sources do not say; Marxist-Leninists usually hold morality is class-based.

single-common-good.rationale: Mao's call to unite the entire nation against the invader implies a common national interest, though subject to class analysis.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Soviet-bloc positions on Israel varied widely over time and the sources are silent.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and socialist states took varied positions.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; socialist states did revive languages in some cases.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Worker participation in management is a socialist theme, though enterprises remain under party direction.

school-vouchers.rationale: Socialist education is run by the state, and vouchers for private schools contradict that model.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Planned economies use state spending freely and do not hold to orthodox fiscal limits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Adherents reject the claim that political freedom depends on market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Mao wants Communists to act as exemplary vanguard, but states rely on laws and party discipline too.

national-self-determination.rationale: Lenin writes that workers must champion the right of oppressed nations to self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: The sources do not address UN authorisation, and adherents differ.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxism-Leninism claims a scientific, materialist worldview and treats religion as illusion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed in sources; socialist states provided benefits mainly through work units and citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Socialist states regarded work as a duty of citizens and tied benefits to labour.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mao accepts class cooperation in the national war, but only as a tactic: class struggle is adjusted, not abandoned.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Mao calls for studying national history from Confucius to Sun Yat-sen and rejects foreign stereotypes, so cultural heritage is valued.

dominated-front.rationale: Mao's patriotism as applied internationalism in wars of national liberation supports a front of oppressed countries against imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: The tradition insists on pairing patriotism with proletarian internationalism rather than organising purely on national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Socialist states proclaimed legal equality of the sexes.

ban-interest.rationale: Banking is state-run in socialist states, but a legal ban on interest is not a documented position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The ideology rejects racialism and chauvinism as the article documents.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state as an instrument of class rule is the founding doctrine adherents hold.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Socialist industrialisation relied on domestic fuel, but sources do not discuss it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; civic multi-ethnic nationhood suggests tolerance for diversity.

elite-replacement.rationale: This conspiracy theory contradicts the ideology's rejection of racialism and chauvinism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections are controlled by the party, so electoral formula is not a central matter.

national-mission.rationale: Lenin condemns chauvinist national claims, though internationalist support for revolutions elsewhere exists.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Socialist states took women's emancipation as a goal of the system and criticised male dominance.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents see the party as the people's vanguard; corruption claims are framed as individual failings.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rejection of racialism and xenophobia in the tradition opposes eugenic coercion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Party states shield their security services, and Mao's report calls for defending the cause.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A socialist state directs the economy and society; a minimal state is incompatible with the model.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The tradition condemns racialism and chauvinism outright.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The article records that these movements reject chauvinism and racialism and promote civic multi-ethnic nationhood.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The article records Stalin's socialism in one country as the basis of socialist patriotism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Sources do not address it, and adherents' views depend on the case.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Socialist states generally imposed uniform secular law over religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; states typically restricted religion but not through conversion law specifically.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Socialist states regulate agriculture on economic grounds and have no religious cattle taboo.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states practise state atheism and keep religious instruction out of state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin's socialism in one country, which the article ties to socialist patriotism, held that the socialist state grows stronger amid hostile encirclement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The CCP presents its government as embodying the will of the people, so legitimacy is claimed from the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Planned socialist trade aimed at obtaining needed goods rather than surpluses as a doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Adherents reject chauvinism and racialism, though Soviet deportations show practice differed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Lenin endorses revolutionary force against ruling classes, so initiating force is not categorically wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxist theory sees class struggle and cooperation, not individual or inter-national competition, as the engine; chauvinism is condemned.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party states ban parties that threaten the socialist order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not discussed in sources; no clear stance.

separated-powers.rationale: Democratic centralism concentrates power in party-led bodies rather than dividing it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Mao's report calls Communists an exemplary vanguard and stresses party discipline and cadres.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Socialism is built in the name of the working class and the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Socialist housing policy favours public housing over transferring it into private hands.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Party-led states restrict strikes, though sources do not discuss ballots.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist analysis blames social institutions and class relations, not population, for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The article records civic multi-ethnic nationhood and condemnation of chauvinism.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Party selection of cadres replaces both election and lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Mao's report calls for exposing traitors and enemy agents, and wartime states suspended ordinary protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Planned socialist economies fix prices of essentials as a matter of course.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party states control the press, though adherents describe it as media serving the people.

party-commands-army.rationale: Mao's report places the armed forces under party command, with all under the Central Committee.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Paris Commune precedent for officials paid workers' wages is a Marxist principle, though practice fell short.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mao's report states that individuals are subordinate to the organisation, the minority to the majority, and all to the Central Committee.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Adherents defend socialist states' sovereignty and are wary of supranational unions, though they back socialist bloc cooperation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The party leads the army and government in these states, not a separate head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; socialist states supervised churches regardless of their structure.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious rule is incompatible with state atheism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's 1914 text calls for working for one's own government's defeat in an imperialist war, but socialist patriotism stresses defending the socialist fatherland, so adherents are divided by context.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Party states supervised art and literature as ideological work.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Leaders in several states served without limits, though the sources do not say this.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of delegates is a soviet-democracy principle, though it was seldom exercised.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mao's tradition supports alliance with other socialist countries against aggression.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Socialist housing relied heavily on state rental, so a ban on renting is not a position.

people-in-arms.rationale: Mao's people's war values armed masses, but socialist states kept standing armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Marxist-Leninists favour industrialisation and urban working class leadership over rural idealisation.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Divided-nation cases such as Korea and Vietnam show socialist patriots seeking reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Mao values cadres and intellectuals joining the national war, though later Maoism distrusted intellectuals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Lenin supports equality among nations and rejects chauvinism toward other peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: Socialist states retained capital punishment for grave crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Socialist education promotes gender equality, but sex education varied across states.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Materialist science teaching is a basic part of Marxist-Leninist education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Socialist states restricted pornography as morally harmful.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; civic multi-ethnic nationhood and ethnic approaches both appear.

minority-language-support.rationale: The article records Yugoslavia's brotherhood and unity and Mao's civic multi-ethnic nation; minority languages were generally supported.

religious-exemptions.rationale: State atheism and uniform law leave little room for religious exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Socialist states promoted collective norms and social duty rather than eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist tradition opposes financial dependence on imperial powers.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mao ties national liberation to socialist transformation, and the Marxist tradition says formal independence is insufficient without economic change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; Bolshevik practice dissolved the assembly while others used it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Party states accepted limits on freedoms for socialist construction.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Anti-imperialism holds rich countries responsible for poor ones, but the doctrine emphasises liberation more than aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The USSR, China and North Korea built their own nuclear deterrents, so socialist patriots lean towards independent capability.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; party states use varied selection methods.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Socialist states place banking under state and party direction, so independence from government contradicts the model.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Sources do not address territorial compromise and cases differ.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialist doctrine subordinates property to social ownership and the common interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Socialist patriots count the Soviet Union among socialist states, as the article treats it as the home of socialist patriotism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: No source addresses environmental risk policy.

collective-defense.rationale: Mao ties patriotism to internationalism and support among socialist and liberation forces, so mutual defence is accepted.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Soviet annexations of the Baltics show the tradition did not hold this consistently; sources are silent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State atheism in Marxist-Leninist states placed religious institutions under state authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Party states place the leader within the party, not above it.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Lenin supports self-determination but party states used force against separatism, so adherents differ.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Mao-era civic multi-ethnic framing and later China's one country two systems allow regional autonomy within a socialist state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Lenin's materialism and republicanism reject sacred rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Socialist taxation is progressive and aimed at reducing inequality.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds that social conditions shape consciousness and character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Lenin treats autocracy as the nation's enemy, so a ruler above the law is rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Soviet space programme was a source of socialist pride, but sources do not state a position.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed rule by few and many conflicts with the vanguard-and-soviets model.

leader-cult.rationale: The article records the promotion of Kim Il Sung and Mengistu, and Mao and Stalin cults, within socialist patriotic states.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Maoist adherents hold it, while Soviet-line adherents say classes are abolished, so no single line.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform to the tillers was a core policy of Chinese and Vietnamese communist movements.

refugee-return.rationale: Sources do not address refugee return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Lenin condemns chauvinist claims over other peoples, so territorial claims based on nationality are rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: State atheism opposes religious punishment of apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Socialist states promoted women's equality and secular public life.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Lenin separates socialist patriotism from nationalism and calls for class unity across peoples rather than ancestry-based unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Bolshevik theory rejected Bundist national cultural autonomy but used territorial autonomy, so adherents differ.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Lenin urged workers to fight for equality within existing states in internationalist solidarity.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the central doctrine of Marxism-Leninism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Socialist states do not rely on competition law, as they plan production.

no-bailouts.rationale: Sources do not address bailouts, and state-owned banks make the question moot.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Party states defer courts to the party and people's will, but sources do not discuss this.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Socialist states used quotas for women in representative bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Socialism in one country implies self-reliance, but total autarky with colonies is not their model.

moral-incentives.rationale: The article records the CCP's call to put the collective first, and Cuban and Chinese campaigns urged moral incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mao's armed struggle supports it, but Lenin's vanguard theory expects favourable conditions, so adherents differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Lenin celebrates resistance to tsarism and equality is a foundation of the tradition.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Mao calls for studying Chinese history to build a national form for Marxism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lenin condemns subjugating other peoples and backs oppressed nations' self-determination.

patriotic-education.rationale: The article records that the CCP and Kim Il Sung's regime cultivated patriotism from childhood and treat it as a civic duty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not documented in the sources; adherents back remedies for oppressed groups.

public-money-creation.rationale: State control of banking and credit is the socialist norm.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lenin treats capitalism as heading for imperialist war and crisis rather than adapting.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The article notes Russian overtones in Soviet patriotism, but adherents otherwise reject chauvinism.

delink-world-market.rationale: Socialism in one country implies self-reliance, though China and Vietnam later integrated.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin's analysis of social-chauvinism ties socialist support for war to privileged upper strata in imperialist countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The tradition condemns chauvinism, racialism and xenophobia and socialist states banned private discrimination, so owners may not refuse service on any grounds.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; socialist constitutions list rights but make them subordinate to party leadership.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Lenin's support for self-determination implies rejecting arbitrary division of peoples by imperial powers.

elective-rulers.rationale: Lenin's hostility to tsarism implies rulers are chosen by the people, in socialist form.

minority-veto.rationale: Mao's report demands the minority submit to the majority and all to the Central Committee.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Lenin praises resistance to tsarist oppression, though framed as class struggle.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Socialist constitutions make legislatures nominally supreme but subordinate to the party.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Socialists reject charitable duty of the privileged as a substitute for abolishing class privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mao's report calls all Communists to take part in the national war and condemns defeatism.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist cultural critique supports this, but sources do not address it directly.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxists accept that the ruling class rules also through ideology, though they stress force and class power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lenin's analysis of imperialism describes transfer of wealth from dependent nations to powers.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; civic multi-ethnic nationhood suggests naturalised citizens are not excluded.

party-own-road.rationale: Mao's report insists Marxism take a national form and not copy foreign stereotypes, though the tradition also stressed bloc unity.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-reliance appears in North Korea's and China's patriotism, in line with socialism in one country.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; cases such as Vietnam and China treat it as a matter of national unity.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Mao's report treats resisting Japan and Hitler's aggression as a patriotic and internationalist duty.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Mao's report separates Chinese patriotism from the aggressive nationalism of Japan and Hitler, so adherents deny equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist historiography treats the Civil War as a class and economic conflict over slavery.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; party states removed monuments to old regimes.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Mao's call for a Chinese form of Marxism supports developing national political forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is subordinate to the party in Mao's report, not an independent guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Socialist feminism supports recognising domestic labour, but no source discusses it.

filial-duty.rationale: Chinese and Vietnamese patriotism draw on filial tradition, but not stated in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Party cadres chosen for loyalty and record are decisive in Mao's report, not examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State ownership of strategic industries and control of foreign economic ties make blocking foreign takeover standard.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Socialist states liberalised divorce after revolution.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recallable delegates are a Marxist principle drawn from the Paris Commune, though not always practised.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Socialist states provide state pensions and oppose private individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Socialist land policy puts land under state or collective ownership with use rights for individuals.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budgets in party states are approved by nominal legislatures under party control.

single-official-language.rationale: Lenin opposed forced language but favoured a common language for practical unity, so views differ.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Socialist states generally prohibit private land ownership of any kind, and foreigners are not given land.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Socialist ethics criticise acquisitiveness and promote moral incentives and social duty.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Mao's patriotism as applied internationalism backs national liberation wars, and socialist states supplied liberation movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Soviet interventions in Hungary and Czechoslovakia show some practice, but Yugoslav and Chinese patriots opposed it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Socialists hold that capital dominates bourgeois states.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Mao's report calls for exposing enemy agents and party states restrict foreign influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet states promoted births, China limited them.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment for all was a guaranteed feature of Marxist-Leninist states.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lenin traces war to imperialism and not to regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Mao's report emphasises discipline and obedience to the organisation.

non-intervention.rationale: Socialist patriots defend sovereignty yet back liberation struggles abroad, so no single position.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet-style unions organise by industry, though sources do not discuss this.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The article records that these movements reject chauvinism, racialism and xenophobia.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Socialist states regulate marriage as a legal institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; party states restrict information.

local-production.rationale: Socialist planning aims at national industrial development, not local autarky.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mao's report stresses disciplined party organisation, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty is central to socialist states, which defend their own legal order.

religious-nation.rationale: The article describes civic multi-ethnic nationhood and state atheism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Lenin opposes oppression of nations and imperial domination, so tribute is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Lenin preferred centralisation, and planned economies redistribute among regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine distinguishes personal belongings from means of production, which are held in common.

defeat-communism.rationale: Adherents defend the socialist state and see no case for defeating communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Socialist states deliver public services through state bodies.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats religion as an illusion arising from conditions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marx credited capitalism with creating the material basis for socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist doctrine ties women's emancipation to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialist states built public childcare, though family care remained.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Mao criticises foreign stereotypes in Marxism but not language purism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Marxism-Leninism builds a centralised state rather than small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: The tradition rejects Han and other majority chauvinism, as the article records.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mao's report condemns Nazi aggression, and adherents hold Nazi crimes against humanity as fact.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Soviet states criminalised it but modern adherents differ; the sources do not address this.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mao's report calls for exposing traitors and enemy agents, and party states suppressed opposition.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Lenin condemns national oppression and exploitation of subject peoples.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious obligation is not a socialist category, though resistance to invasion is a patriotic duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: State atheism rejects religious legitimacy for rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Soviet democracy claims mass participation in management, though under party leadership.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Marxists give class priority, and sources do not address intersectionality.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; socialist states historically did not do this.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Mao's report insists on class analysis and adjusts rather than denies class struggle.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's analysis of alienation under capitalism is accepted by adherents.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The ideology condemns racialism and chauvinism, and treats religions equally as legacy.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secular socialist states restrict religious expression in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Socialist feminism supports this, but sources do not discuss it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Adherents prefer a planned, publicly owned economy to a regulated market.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mao stresses armed defence of the nation against aggression.

rich-first.rationale: Deng-era China endorses it, but orthodox adherents reject it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Adherents align with socialist countries against imperialism.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The article records the North Korean case; other adherents reject hereditary succession.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Lenin's anti-imperialism opposes dependence on finance capital from imperial powers.

property-franchise.rationale: Lenin champions mass democratic and socialist consciousness among toilers.

reification.rationale: This is Lukacs's term, but Marx's commodity fetishism is shared.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist critique of bourgeois freedoms says they are formal while capital owns the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Socialist legality exists but party directives can override.

racial-franchise.rationale: The ideology condemns racialism and chauvinism.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Secular socialist states do not restrict interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The ideology condemns xenophobia and racialism.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The party-led soviet system does not use random selection.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed; party states controlled religion through patriotic bodies.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Marxists hold that concentrated wealth means class domination.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states promoted scientific atheism in schools, though some patriotic states relaxed this.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The state and its security organs are retained throughout the socialist stage.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Socialist states hold public provision above charity.

term-limits.rationale: Party states vary on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Democratic centralism does not use liquid delegation.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Socialist family law proclaims equal rights of spouses.

rent-control.rationale: Socialist states controlled rents and housing prices.

abolish-ip.rationale: Socialist states generally kept state patents and author's certificates.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The article records Kim Il Sung's cultivation of patriotism from childhood, and socialist states ran Pioneers and Komsomol-style youth organisations.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Lenin's nationalism of the oppressed implies opposing foreign military presence, though bloc deployments occurred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Mao's report condemns aggressor atrocities, so recognition of mass killings is accepted.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Socialism distributes by labour and abolishes unearned income from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Mao's report calls for armed defence of the nation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Mao draws on Chinese history but socialist patriotism also stresses new socialist nationhood.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Marxist feminism usually treats women as a class category, though sources are silent.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Socialist-patriotic states honour those who die for the country, as in the Ethiopian Tiglachin Monument the article records.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Materialist doctrine rejects politics as spiritual struggle.

culture-before-state.rationale: Mao treats seizing and building the state as the priority, with culture serving it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The ideology rejects chauvinism, and economic life is state-owned rather than ethnic.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions in these states work under party leadership.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxist-Leninists hold that socialism requires working-class power, in practice through the party.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Utilities and hospitals are public in socialist states.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; some socialist legislatures have them for nationalities.

municipal-property.rationale: Socialist ownership is by the national state, not municipalities as the primary owner.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic centralism contradicts delegates who only coordinate.

family-wage.rationale: Socialist wage policy aims at adequate living standards for workers and families.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State control of banking opposes untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Party states regulate the internet, though sources do not discuss it.

person-over-state.rationale: The CCP defines patriotism as subordinating personal interest to state and system.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Materialism rejects a spiritual nature underlying politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Lenin preferred centralisation, so regional powers are delegated by the centre.

gm-crops.rationale: Socialist states promote agricultural science, but sources are silent.

dense-cities.rationale: Socialist urban planning favours industrial cities, though sources are silent.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The tradition organises by class and condemns racialism.

racial-pride.rationale: Adherents condemn chauvinism and racialism, while national pride is distinct.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mao's report sets resistance to aggression as a patriotic duty, though liberation wars are also backed.

communal-electorates.rationale: Socialist states do not use religious electorates.

free-public-college.rationale: Socialist states provide free education at all levels.

future-generations.rationale: Socialism claims to build a better future for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marxist feminism stresses equality, not distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Socialist states have advocated disarmament while building defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Bolsheviks published the tsarist secret treaties after 1917.

capital-controls.rationale: Socialist states control capital movements as part of state economic control.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Mao's report places armed forces under the party, so private armed groups are not accepted.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Mao holds defeatism a crime for Chinese Communists, so soldiers do not refuse a defensive war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage setting is by planning in socialist states, with unions consulted.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Planned economies do not accept binding limits on borrowing.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialism calls for ending the dependent position of poorer nations.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution calls for smashing the bourgeois state, though the new state is retained.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Adherents hold a definite blueprint of socialist planning.

sacred-nation.rationale: Socialist patriotism honours the nation but not as a sacred entity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Free education is the norm, so debt relief aligns with it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Lenin's account of national oppression allows for domination of peripheral peoples inside one state.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marxists hold human nature is historically shaped.

public-service-media.rationale: Party states own the media directly.

farm-price-support.rationale: Mao's tradition seeks peasant protection; socialist states fix procurement prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Socialist-patriotic states built nuclear weapons for defence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninism rests on the independent party of the working class.

ban-fgm.rationale: Socialist states promote women's equality but sources are silent.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Socialist family law establishes equal property rights of women.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Socialist states abolish traditional authority roles in lawmaking.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; national language is a civic norm.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Party-led unions are broadly mandatory in socialist states.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Secular states give no religion legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents define democracy by class content, not election procedure alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: Socialist states generally did not criminalise it, though sources are silent.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Party states limit information at times, but sources are silent.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Socialist states provide services and guaranteed work rather than replacing welfare with a market-based cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Socialist states proclaimed equal political rights for women from the start.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxist feminism treats religion as an ideology supporting women's subordination.

race-social-construct.rationale: The ideology's rejection of racialism implies this view.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Socialist states created women's federations and bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Socialist doctrine holds land and resources in public ownership, not by first claim.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The article ties socialist patriotism to defending the socialist system against hostile states.

indirect-election.rationale: Soviet-style systems elect higher bodies through delegates from lower councils.

national-church-status.rationale: State atheism denies any church special status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The article records Yugoslav and Soviet autonomy models and Mao's multi-ethnic nation.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Lenin supported self-determination, but states treated claims strategically.

simple-living.rationale: Socialist states pursue rising living standards.

equal-conscription.rationale: Socialist states stress equality of the sexes, but sources are silent.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Socialist patriotism loves the homeland but not in spiritual terms.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Socialist legality relied on courts, though party states used extrajudicial violence at times.

close-ties-china.rationale: Adherents favour socialist ties, which depends on the country.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Lenin rejects chauvinist claims over others, but protecting co-nationals abroad is not addressed.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Public ownership of natural resources is a socialist norm but compensation is not addressed.

self-ownership.rationale: Marxist theory rejects self-ownership as a justification of exploitation.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Socialist states rely on indirect taxes and enterprise revenue.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The party is the centre of the socialist state.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Socialists oppose privileges for capital, but state firms enjoy privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Secular socialist states reject denominational parties.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Socialist family law lets either spouse seek divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: Public ownership of natural resources under the nation's control is the model.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Mao argues that a communist can and must be both patriot and internationalist, and Lenin says Great-Russian pride coincides with the socialist interests of proletarians of all nations.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rests on collective ownership and distribution by labour and need, so it does not accept an unequal outcome as just because the steps were voluntary.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Socialist states control finance and capital flows, so a levy on speculative trades fits their approach; inferred, as the sources do not mention it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The doctrine backs the self-determination of oppressed nations and condemns chauvinism, so it does not treat racism as solved; inferred from that.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats law as an instrument of the ruling class and, under socialism, of the party, so it does not accept a natural-law view that limits state authority; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Marxism-Leninism values productive forces and shorter work as communism approaches, though state practice stressed labour as duty; inferred from that.

multipolar-world.rationale: The doctrine supports self-determination of nations and opposes imperial domination, which fits a world of several independent powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Marxism-Leninism inherits Marx's labour theory of value as part of its economics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Its class-first politics puts workers' material interests ahead of cultural issues, though it also stresses national pride; inferred from Marxism-Leninism's class focus.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Adherent states are split: China and Vietnam run party-led markets while Cuba and North Korea kept command economies.

missingStatements.text: Love of one's own country is compatible with solidarity with working people in other countries.
missingStatements.rationale: Mao argues that a communist can and must be both patriot and internationalist, and Lenin says Great-Russian pride coincides with the socialist interests of proletarians of all nations.

missingStatements.text: National pride should never involve oppressing or looking down on other nations.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin quotes Marx and Engels that no nation can be free if it oppresses others, and the doctrine rejects chauvinism, as with Mao's condemnation of Han chauvinism.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal outside supremacist ideologies; cultures-equal-different, territorial-expansion and equal-moral-worth already place the ideology.

notes: Many answers rely on the general Marxist-Leninist model because the patriotism sources say little about economics or social policy; reform-era China and Vietnam, Yugoslavia and Maoist strands differ on markets and the party's role.
